title: 1665 in London's death records
hook: Yearly records of London's deaths run from 1629 to 1710. What did 1665 look like?

doesNotKnow: how a year's burials compare with normal
that the city's own weekly bills let us see it

misconception: Epidemics raise deaths a little; "the plague year" means somewhat more deaths than usual.
objective: The learner can say that London's recorded burials in 1665 were about six times the year before, mostly put down to plague, and that burials fell back the next year.

claims.text: Where it stops: these are recorded deaths and recorded causes, from later compilations (Creighton; Campbell).
claims.source: CRAN HistData man/Arbuthnot.Rd (opened by FC43, FC45): Plague and Mortality are 'deaths from the plague and total mortality obtained by Campbell and from Creighton (1965)'; references Creighton, C. (1965), A History of Epidemics in Britain, 2nd edition, and Campbell (2001). Both are long after 1710 ('later'). The sentence is FC45 fix (a): it holds whether Campbell took the columns from Creighton or the two are separate sources.
claims.note: FC pass 39 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Depends on what a Bill recorded: burials, with causes entered by non-medical searchers. No source for that could be opened (see c1). The source field already offers cutting 'or a doctor's diagnosis'. | FC pass 41 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): VERIFIED. Learner text: 'Where it stops: these are recorded burials and recorded causes, not a count of every death or a doctor's diagnosis.' Opened: Lancet 2020 (PMC7154511): 'The searchers were not medical professionals: rather, they were usually pairs of older women who were recipients of parish money, and their job was to determine the cause of death', and the clerks reported 'Christenings and Burials'. Cureus 2026 (PMC13244054): 'Nonconformists, Jews, and unbaptized infants were often excluded from the Church of England burial system and, therefore, underrepresented'; causes were 'certified by searchers of the dead and recorded by parish clerks'. Hist Psychiatry 2012 (PMC3764771), quoting Black 1789: deaths 'interred in dissenting and unregistered burying grounds, or in other places of interment without the verge of the bills' were not reported. So burials, not every death, and lay causes, not a doctor's diagnosis. | FC pass 43 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): DISPUTED. Was 'Where it stops: these are recorded burials and recorded causes, not a count of every death or a doctor's diagnosis.' Support changed from convention to source (the Rd), since the Bills-based basis no longer applies. Reset to unverified for a fact-checker who is not the builder. | FC pass 45 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15, W-980): UNVERIFIED. Learner text (reveal): 'Where it stops: these are recorded deaths and recorded causes, from one later compilation (Creighton).' 'Recorded deaths and recorded causes' and 'later' are supported: the Rd (CRAN HistData_1.1.1.tar.gz man/Arbuthnot.Rd, opened) calls the columns 'total mortality' and 'deaths from plague', and both Creighton (1965 edition) and Campbell (2001) are long after 1710. 'One ... compilation (Creighton)' is not supported. The Rd says the columns were 'obtained by Campbell and from Creighton (1965)' and lists both works. Read as 'Campbell obtained them from Creighton', Creighton is the one compilation. Read as two sources, 'one' is wrong. The Rd does not settle which. The one page that would settle it, Campbell's arbuth.html (math.uni.edu), returned 403 from this host; archive.org, JSTOR and Crossref were blocked too. Fix (builder), either: (a) word it to what the Rd says under both readings: 'Where it stops: these are recorded deaths and recorded causes, from later compilations (Creighton; Campbell).'; or (b) a session that can open math.uni.edu/~campbell/arbuth.html or Campbell 2001 (Human Biology 73(4)) confirms that Campbell took both columns from Creighton; the current sentence then verifies as written. | v4 (demo-builder, 2026-10-15, W-992): FC45 fix (a) applied verbatim. Was 'Where it stops: these are recorded deaths and recorded causes, from one later compilation (Creighton).'; now 'Where it stops: these are recorded deaths and recorded causes, from later compilations (Creighton; Campbell).'. 'Later': Creighton's 2nd edition is dated 1965 in the Rd and Campbell's article 2001, both long after the 1629-1710 records. 'Compilations (Creighton; Campbell)', plural with both names, holds under both readings FC45 identified (Campbell took the columns from Creighton, or two separate sources): it claims no more than that the numbers reached the data set through these two later works. Under the first reading 'compilations' slightly overstates Campbell's role, but the sentence names both works the Rd credits, so I do not count it as false. recall.question: A town normally records 100 deaths a year. One year it records 600, and 450 of those from one cause. What share is that cause?
recall.why: 450 of 600 is 75%: the share is out of that year's total, not the normal year's.
